subject: Escape velocity offer and runtime tradeoffs
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@skyline.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re-evaluating runtime + pricing — data attached

Olga / Connor,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier this week. We're mid-renewal and have a competing supplier (unnamed in the RFP) that just surfaced a 15-20% list discount across our projected usage. Before we go down the path of a formal RFP, I wanted to share Skyline's usage snapshot and a short sense of what would keep us with Redwood:

- A bridge that neutralizes the first 3–6 months of delta while we validate runtime economics.
- Clear committed performance SLA (99.9% for token latency under 300ms for our P99 flows).
- Packaging clarity for reserved capacity vs consumption so we can model costs.

Attaching: usage_report_q1.csv and RFP_Skyline_2027.pdf (redacted).

If Redwood can propose a short-term migration subsidy and an accelerated onboarding window (2 weeks), we will fold that into our commercial evaluation. Can you send a couple of concrete options (term sheet-level) for us to review by EOD next week?

Sofia (procurement) is copied; feel free to include any benchmarks or model-level cost assumptions.

Best,
Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform Engineering, Skyline AI

---
Attachments: usage_report_q1.csv (csv), RFP_Skyline_2027.pdf (pdf)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@skyline.ai>
Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.com, jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating runtime + pricing — data attached

Alex — thanks for the context and the files. Appreciate the upfront signal on the competitor discount.

High-level, we can do two actionable packages that target the outcomes you listed:

1) FastTrack Subsidy (aimed at minimizing short-term churn risk)
   - 3-month migration subsidy (applied as credits) sized to neutralize a 20% list delta on forecasted usage (~$150k).
   - Dedicated onboarding engineering (2-week SLA on onboarding tasks) and one-week performance tuning sprint.
   - Conditional 6-month 10% list discount on committed reserved units if you convert to Dedicated.

2) Ops+Conserve (aimed at long-term unit-econ improvement)
   - No upfront subsidy. Instead offer quantization and KV-cache tuning package + 30% estimated per-token cost reduction after 3 months of pilot tuning.
   - 90-day pilot with measured per-token baseline & post-optimization projection.

Connor will sketch expected per-token math and assumptions; Jasmine will follow with a term-sheet PDF for FastTrack. If neither is a fit we can also propose a hybrid (partial credit + pilot).

Next steps: I'll put together the FastTrack term sheet and estimate credits against your Q1 snapshot; can we aim to share that by Wednesday?

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

Olga — appreciate the two options. A couple of clarifying points from procurement and infra: 

- If Redwood wants to win this, procurement will still need an economic parity to the competitor's 20% off list across at least a 6-month window, or a firm migration subsidy that guarantees zero additional spend vs incumbent for our first two quarters.
- We also need explicit rollback language in the event the pilot fails to meet the 99.9% latency SLO for our P99 scoring flows.
- Term length is flexible but preference leans to a 12–18 month initial commitment if we get parity or subsidy.

Sofia: happy to follow up with specific procurement language.

If you can share an illustrative matrix with net effective price (post-credits) and the fallback/rollback clause, we can put this to our buying committee.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Re-evaluating runtime + pricing — data attached

Alex / Sofia — looping in proposed term sheet and two concrete options. See attached fasttrack_term_sheet.pdf. Summary below.

Option A — FastTrack (accelerate commit)
- Migration subsidy: $150,000 credit applied across first invoice cycles (stacked against usage).
- 6-month net parity guard: if average quarterly spend > competitor-adjusted forecast, Redwood will issue an additional one-time credit up to 50% of the difference.
- Dedicated onboarding and one SRE onsite-week (remote) during go-live.
- Rollback: 30-day notice and data export assistance; no early-termination penalty for failure to meet agreed P99 SLO in two consecutive weeks during pilot.

Option B — Pilot+Optimize (econ-first)
- 90-day pilot, no upfront subsidy. Redwood implements cache/quantization and provides a post-pilot model for projected per-token savings.
- If pilot achieves >=20% effective unit-econ improvement, Redwood will apply a conversion credit equal to 25% of the first quarter's invoiced usage.

We've attached a short term sheet (fasttrack_term_sheet.pdf) with the language you asked for. If you like Option A we can route a short sideletter for signature and provision the dedicated onboarding immediately.

-Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (212) 555-0277

Alex — quick note on the per-token modeling so everyone has the same assumptions. Attached is a simple workbook (per_token_modeling.xlsx) that walks through:

- Baseline: current consume-on-demand pricing @ Redwood hosted (list) + expected P50/P95 token mix from your Q1 export.
- Optimized: model-level quantization (4-bit), prefix caching and batch tuning under the FastTrack onboarding run.
- Assumptions: 25% KV cache hit rate after tuning, 30% inference kernel win for our recommended model family, estimated reserved discount applied in FastTrack flows.

Net effective examples in the sheet show how the $150k subsidy + reserved conversion result in net parity or slightly better in months 1–6 for a typical Skyline profile. If you want, we can run the workbook against your actual daily sequence-length distribution — need a redacted sample trace for that.

Connor O'Brien

Folks — after internal review, procurement is willing to move forward with Option A (FastTrack) provided the following are agreed in a short sideletter:

1) Migration subsidy fixed at $150,000 applied as credits on first three invoices.
2) 99.9% P99 latency SLO for our prime production routes as defined in the term sheet; two-week remediation window before rollback protections trigger.
3) 12-month initial contract term with an option to convert to dedicated reserved capacity after month 3 at the discounted rates listed.

If you can send the sideletter and DocuSign link today we will table this with legal and procurement for final sign-off.

Appreciate everyone's speed on this — looks promising.

Best,
Alex
